evidence.correctness: Downloaded the cached GoEmotions CSV and ran `python3 experiments/run.py`: results.txt regenerated byte-identically (git status clean), figure.py also unchanged. Then wrote an independent script (indep2.py in the scratchpad: own csv loader, own replay of the seeded shuffle, own register regex, own lexicon matcher, own multinomial NB, own confusion counts and numpy PPI/Monte Carlo with a different RNG). Reproduced split 3188 (1886 formal / 1302 informal), prevalences 0.2587/0.2442 and true gap -0.01451; lexicon error 0.2121/0.2120 and NB error 0.2821/0.2627 with the same sens/spec; naive gaps -0.04306 (NB) and -0.00465 (lexicon); coverage NB naive 0.000, PPI 0.949 (reported 0.956), lexicon naive 1.000, PPI 0.971 (0.968); E3 flag rates 0.052-0.059 (NB) and 0.031-0.043 (lexicon) vs reported 0.045-0.065 and 0.025: within Monte Carlo error. The 8,000-item approximation reproduces as 8,221 per group. All reported numbers are right for the stated model. Not 4 because the interpretation of the E3 null rests on an effect that is not itself significant (see claims).

Six hand-seeded mutations in qualregister.py, each reverted (git status clean afterwards): z-statistic denominator 1/n2 -> 1/n1 SURVIVED; error counted as agreement (!= -> ==) SURVIVED; dropping abs(), isupper->isalpha, dropping the closing-quote regex branch, and z=1.0 were caught. 4 of 6 caught; the two survivors sit in the headline computation (the error count and the z denominator). No test pins results.txt/README tables to run.py. This is the binding gate.
evidence.craft: Read qualregister.py (53 lines), test_qualregister.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, and the qual-real/qual-correction modules it reuses. Clean, documented, stdlib only, deterministic seeds, reuses estimators instead of copying them (good). Defects: the sys.path hack and shadowed `run` module name; z test ignores the finite-population correction; no input validation (e.g. an unknown group key in audit_detects raises KeyError; greedy rng.sample raises if n_gold > n); tests are few and equal-n only.
evidence.claims: Checked README claims against files: every table number matches results.txt; the 'coders are not LLMs' and 'register is a proxy' limits are prominent and correct; the 'Produced with AI assistance' note is present. Gaps: the headline 'could not detect the small difference that was there' treats a 1.9-point difference as real, but a full-sample z test on all 3,188 items gives z = -1.21 (p about 0.23); finite-population sampling makes flag rates look lower than nominal; the '~1 min' runtime is 1.8 s cached. The limitations section partly concedes the sampling error, so this is a wording and framing problem, not a wrong number. Kept at 3 because the claims are caveated in the same README and every number checks.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can reproduce and extend this (shared loader, seeds, stdlib), and qual-gate already built on it, but the finding is a null on a typographic proxy with two stand-in coders: it tells a qualitative-coding researcher little about LLM coders or about dialect, the question the track is about. The real contribution, that overall-error audits at ordinary n are low-powered, is a known property of two-proportion tests, shown here on one corpus. 2.
evidence.domain: A psychometrician or a computational social scientist would compare against differential item functioning / differential misclassification practice: test sensitivity and specificity by group (not overall error), report effect sizes with intervals or an equivalence margin, and cite the dialect-bias literature (Blodgett et al. 2016; Sap et al. 2019) and LLM-annotation validation (Egami et al. 2023; Hopkins and King 2010; Gilardi et al. 2023). The README cites none of the dialect/bias work, uses a z test on pooled error, and uses a typography proxy for register. The PPI half is sound and standard (Angelopoulos 2023). Departures acknowledged only partly. 2.

defects.what: Headline says a hand-coded sample 'could not detect the small difference that was there', but the naive-Bayes 1.9-point error difference is itself not statistically distinguishable from zero on all 3,188 items (z = -1.21, p about 0.23). Power numbers are quoted against an effect that may be noise; the 8,000-item figure inherits this. The README's limitations section partly concedes sampling error but not this.

Audit test is a pooled z on the overall error rate between two register groups; the practitioner's concern is differential sensitivity/specificity, bias in the group gap, or equivalence within a margin (the README itself proposes the sensitivity-based audit as a next step). A null on the weaker test is then read as 'an ordinary audit cannot see differential error'. Prior differential-misclassification and measurement-error literature (Blodgett 2016, Sap 2019, Egami 2023, Hopkins and King 2010, Gilardi 2023) is not cited; novelty is not stated against it.

Core audit code is under-tested: a seeded se typo (1/n2 -> 1/n1) and a sign flip that counts agreements as errors both pass all 4 tests (2 of 6 seeded mutations survive); the z test is only checked with equal group sizes, and audit_detects/detection_rate are checked only at two extreme cases.

Subsamples of up to 800 are drawn without replacement from a 3,188-item population (25%) and the pooled z ignores the finite-population correction, so flag rates are biased low relative to an infinite population (NB n=800: 0.059 vs 0.080 with replacement); the README reads them as the nominal 5% false-positive rate.
Reproduce section says '~1 min' for run.py; with the CSV cached it takes 1.8 s. No test pins results.txt or the README tables to run.py output.

Single seed, single split and 200 draws per E3 cell (se about 0.015), so cells 0.025 to 0.065 cannot be told apart; the 0.025/0.030 lexicon cells are described as 'at or below 5%' without a stated reading.

Experiments reach into ../qual-real/experiments by sys.path and import its run.py under the name run (shadows this folder's own run.py); fragile coupling, and qualregister.py re-exports r and q via import side effects.

verdict: Every number reproduces: results.txt and the figure regenerate byte-identically, and an independent loader, coders and Monte Carlo (own code, different RNG) match the register split, error rates, sensitivities, naive and PPI gap coverage, flag rates and the 8,000-item approximation. The work is honest about its limits (not an LLM, register is a proxy). It does not meet the bar because verification is 2: 2 of 6 seeded mutations survived the 4 tests, including one that counts agreements as errors and one that corrupts the z denominator, i.e. the headline computation. Beyond that, the headline reads a null on a 1.9-point error difference as 'could not detect the difference that was there' when that difference is itself not significant on all 3,188 items (z = -1.21); the audit tests pooled error rather than group sensitivity/specificity or equivalence; and the dialect-bias and annotation-validation literature (Blodgett, Sap, Egami, Hopkins and King, Gilardi) is not cited. Worst defect: the overclaim about a difference that may be noise, plus the untested core. Fitness and domain are 2: a reproducible, correctly computed teaching-level study, not yet publishable research.
